pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Michigan Electrical Journeyman examination is administered by PSI for candidates approved through the State of Michigan Bureau of Construction Codes. The Department determines license eligibility, and approved candidates receive instructions to pay for and schedule the examination with PSI. The Michigan Electrical Journeyman exam includes 80 questions, requires a 75% minimum passing score, and allows 150 minutes of testing time. The exam is computer-based and is offered through PSI testing centers. Candidates receive score information after completing the examination. The examination is designed to test a candidate’s knowledge of Michigan’s skilled trades regulation act, rules under that act, current electrical code rules, the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, applicable adopted codes, and the electrical theory related to those codes.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Michigan Electrical Journeyman exam is an open book test. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references to the examination center. Approved references include the National Electrical Code, 2016 PA 407, 1972 PA 230, and Michigan Electrical Code Rules Part 8. The National Electrical Code book used in the examination may have factory markings or highlights with factory tabs only. Other editions of the NEC may be used during the examination, but the exam questions are based on the code edition identified by the testing provider for the exam. The NEC Handbook is not allowed in the examination room. All reference material must be bound. Materials printed from the Bureau of Construction Codes website must be bound by three staples on the left edge in separate documents. Highlighting, marking, and tabs in printed documents are not permitted. Candidates may not bring additional loose or attached papers with approved references. Candidates may not write, highlight, underline, or index references during the exam.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Michigan journeyman electrician licensing begins with meeting the state’s apprentice, experience, and application requirements. Candidates must apply through the Bureau of Construction Codes, be approved by the Department, schedule the examination through PSI, pass the Electrical Journeyman exam, and complete any remaining licensing steps required by the state. A typical Michigan journeyman electrician path includes registering as an electrical apprentice, gaining qualifying supervised experience, maintaining documentation of work hours and supervision, completing any applicable classroom or training requirements, submitting the examination application and fees to the Department, receiving approval to test, scheduling with PSI, passing the exam, and completing license issuance requirements. Michigan requires the Department to determine a candidate’s eligibility before the candidate schedules the licensing examination. Once the Department approves the candidate for the exam, PSI receives the approval information and provides instructions for payment and scheduling.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Journeyman candidates are limited to two exam attempts within one year of eligibility and must reapply with the state if the attempt limit or eligibility period is exceeded. Candidates should keep accurate records of apprentice registration, work history, supervising license information, employment dates, job duties, training records, and any education used for credit. Complete documentation can make the state application process easier and help avoid delays.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Michigan issues electrical journeyman licenses through the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under the state electrical licensing framework. An individual must be at least 20 years old and must meet the statutory requirements for an electrical journeyman license. The standard experience pathway requires at least 8,000 hours of experience obtained over at least four years. The experience must be related to electrical construction or maintenance of buildings, electrical wiring, or electrical equipment, and it must be performed under the direct supervision of an individual licensed under Michigan’s electrical licensing law. Michigan also recognizes a pathway involving completion of a recognized training or education program that is equivalent to 8,000 hours of experience, along with a minimum required amount of experience under the direct supervision of a licensed individual. Applicants using education or training credit should organize documentation carefully because the Department reviews eligibility before authorizing examination.

pieces.t: After a candidate passes the examination, the Department completes the licensing process according to state requirements. pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The Michigan master electrician licensing process begins with meeting the state’s eligibility requirements. A candidate must be at least 22 years old, must have the required supervised electrical experience, and must have held a journeyperson electrician license for the required period. Candidates should make sure their experience records are accurate and properly documented before applying. After confirming eligibility, the candidate applies through the Michigan Bureau of Construction Codes licensing process. The application may require personal information, license history, experience documentation, and other materials required by the state. Michigan reviews the application and determines whether the candidate qualifies for examination and licensure. Once approved, the candidate follows the examination scheduling instructions provided through the approved testing process.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Michigan uses a state-level electrical licensing structure. The Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, Bureau of Construction Codes, administers electrical licensing and regulates license classifications including journeyperson electrician, master electrician, and electrical contractor. Candidates pursuing a Michigan Master Electrician license should follow the state licensing process rather than a local-only license path. The Michigan master electrician license is an advanced license for experienced electrical professionals. To qualify, applicants must meet the age requirement, supervised experience requirement, and journeyperson licensure requirement established by the state. Master electrician candidates should be prepared to demonstrate advanced knowledge of electrical construction, wiring, equipment, maintenance, code compliance, and state electrical rules. Michigan also regulates electrical contracting separately. A master electrician license does not automatically function as an electrical contractor license.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Effective Michigan Master Electrician exam preparation should include code review, calculation practice, reference navigation, Michigan electrical rule review, and repeated exposure to exam-style questions. The NEC is detailed, and candidates need to understand how to use it as a working reference. Study time should focus on learning where information is located, how code sections connect, and how to apply the rule to the facts in the question. The 2026 Michigan Master Electrician Study Guide supports topic-by-topic review. Candidates can use it to organize study around major knowledge areas instead of jumping randomly through the code. A strong study routine may include reading one topic, locating related NEC sections, answering practice questions, reviewing missed answers, and returning to the code book to understand the correct reasoning. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is important because calculation questions can be challenging under exam pressure.

pieces.t: Candidates should practice conductor ampacity, temperature correction, adjustment factors, box fill, raceway fill, service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit requirements, motor full-load current, overcurrent protection, transformer sizing, voltage drop, and demand factors. During study, candidates should practice locating definitions, general installation rules, conductor sizing requirements, grounding and bonding provisions, service and feeder rules, motor provisions, wiring method articles, equipment requirements, special occupancies, and special equipment rules. The goal is to become comfortable moving through the code quickly and accurately. The 2026 Master Electrician Flash Cards provide a practical way to reinforce key facts through repetition.
